paper_title: VideoLLaMB Long-context Video Understanding with Recurrent Memory   Bridges
caption: GPU Memory Cost. We apply all the experiments on a single NVIDIA A800 GPU.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates GPU memory cost (in GB) as a function of the number of video frames for several models, with multiple colored line series shown together for comparison. The x-axis is labeled “Number of Frames,” uses a linear scale, and spans roughly 0 to just over 1000 frames, with labeled ticks at 0, 200, 400, 600, 800, and 1000. The y-axis is labeled “Memory (GB),” uses a linear scale, and spans roughly 0 to a bit above 400 GB, with labeled ticks at 0, 50, 100, 150, 200, 250, 300, 350, and 400. The VideoLLAVA series is drawn in purple with circular markers and a solid line, rising steeply from about 20–30 GB at very low frame counts (near the left edge) to about 65 GB around 64 frames, about 120 GB at 128 frames, about 230 GB at 256 frames, and then reaching beyond the top of the plotted y-range (above 400 GB) by roughly 320 frames. The LLaVA-NeXT series is drawn in blue/teal with circular markers and a solid line, increasing from roughly 18–22 GB at very low frame counts to about 30 GB at 128 frames, about 45 GB at 256 frames, about 75 GB at 512 frames, and about 145 GB at 1024 frames. The PLLaVA series is drawn in green with circular markers and a solid line, increasing from roughly 16–20 GB at very low frame counts to about 24 GB at 128 frames, about 30 GB at 256 frames, about 45 GB at 512 frames, and about 75 GB at 1024 frames. The VideoLLaMB-R series is drawn in mustard/gold with circular markers and a solid line, increasing gradually from roughly 15–17 GB at very low frame counts to about 18 GB at 128 frames, about 21 GB at 256 frames, about 27 GB at 512 frames, and about 38 GB at 1024 frames. The legend also lists a VideoLLaMB series (pink/red), but a distinct corresponding line is not clearly visible in the plotting area.
